Yes—[RecPO (ACL 2026)](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.656.pdf) provides experimental evidence for preference intensity and interaction recency in LLM preference optimization. Table 2 compares no adaptive margins, intensity-only margins, and intensity-plus-recency margins across five datasets. Intensity improves Hit@1 throughout; adding recency improves four datasets, with BeerAdvocate an exception. This supports its particular training objective, not a universal recency mechanism. Its rating-based intensity experiments also rely on information unavailable in this RecHarness task; interaction histories alone do not establish preference intensity.

I found no direct published validation that frozen-model context-ablation sensitivity predicts gains from context dropout or relative-bias regularization in HSTU. Related evidence is narrower: [Recency Dropout for Recurrent Recommender Systems](https://arxiv.org/html/2201.11016) reports simulation, offline, and live benefits from removing recent activities during RNN training, with Jacobian analysis of learned dependencies. [Measuring Recency Bias](https://arxiv.org/html/2409.09722) studies last-item recommendation frequency, a different diagnostic. Neither establishes the proposed sensitivity-to-training-benefit relationship. Frozen ablations measure an existing model’s dependence under input perturbation; interpreting that dependence as remediable overreliance remains a hypothesis.

Recommended design: specify the sensitivity measure and directional hypothesis before trials; retrain matched baseline, dropout-only, bias-regularization-only, and combined HSTU variants, keeping seeds, compute limits, splits, and candidates fixed. Select using the host’s four-category macro validation HR@10, report category results and paired user-level uncertainty, and reserve hidden test evaluation for the final selected configuration. Establishing sensitivity as a predictor additionally requires diagnostic discovery and confirmation on disjoint allowed validation subsets or independent datasets; selection on the same validation set remains exploratory. Sensitivity justifies an experiment, not an expected improvement.
